interpretation: The hand-filled baseline was NOT the weaker side on declarative facts: 0 omissions across inputs, outputs, injected dependencies, fields, methods and lifecycle hooks in both components. What the extractor uniquely supplies is DERIVED and cross-cutting -- template-to-method call edges no reader enumerated by hand. What it still misses is cross-unit, which Phase 2 owns. The comparison's real yield was two extractor defects, one of which the LLM had gotten right.
caveats: Two components, one repository, JHipster-generated -- generated code is more regular than hand-written code.
The baseline predates D12/D12a/D13 and is at schemaVersion 0.2.0; only categories present on both sides were compared.
'LLM missed' counts facts the extractor found and the hand-fill did not. It is not a measure of requirement.md quality, which F1 scored separately.
